text:
Alex: Heads up — noticed p99 on api-gateway jump from ~90ms to ~380ms around 16:05. CPU on telemetry-sidecar is pegged.
telemetry-bot: [alert] exporter-sidecar cpu=87% write_latency_p99=420ms span_ingest_rate=12k/s
Priya: ugh. Any recent rollouts to instrumentation?
Alex: We rolled a change to add detailed span annotations for db calls ~16:00 (marcos's change). Could be volume/size.
Marcos: That was just adding 3 fields to spans for query_plan_id + planner_flags. They shouldn't be huge.
Jia: Can you dump a span size sample from the sidecar?
Alex: grabbing a few from the sidecar logs now. snippet:
```
span_id=0x1a2 attr_count=12 size_bytes=860
span_id=0x1a3 attr_count=18 size_bytes=1240
span_id=0x1a4 attr_count=25 size_bytes=1780
```
Priya: 1.7KB per span avg seems high — we typically see ~400-600b. If batch sizes are fixed by bytes, exporter flushes more often which increases syscall/CPU.
Marcos: Hmm those 3 new fields are strings with the whole query plan encoded as json in one case (oops). I assumed a plan id but it turned into the whole plan object.
Jia: That explains size. Can we roll that PR back or at least stop serializing the plan?
Marcos: I can push a revert but want to check traffic patterns. The spike correlates with a rollout to canary group at 16:00.
Alex: For immediate mitigation can we increase the batching threshold on exporter from 1MB to 4MB so we reduce flush frequency?
Priya: We can, but that will raise memory pressure on sidecar pod. Currently memory usage is 1.2GB.
Jia: Short checklist: 1) throttle sample rate, 2) increase batch byte threshold temporarily, 3) revert plan payload. Which is fastest?
Marcos: I can revert the instrumentation PR in ~5m. Meanwhile Priya, can you try bumping exporter batch_bytes in config?
Priya: Doing a staged rollout to 2x (1MB -> 2MB) on canaries first. deploy-bot: started config rollout telemetry/exporter/batch_bytes=2097152 to telemetry-sidecar, 3 pods at a time.
telemetry-bot: [metric] exporter_batch_flush_count ↓ after config change (canary) — will watch cpu.
Alex: After the canary bump cpu dropped from 87% -> 62% on canary pods, p99 on the canary-backed gateway routes down to ~150ms. Good sign.
Jia: Nice. Still need a full fix though — keeping long JSON in span attrs is brittle. Marcos, please revert and update to only send plan_id (string).
Marcos: On it. I'll open a follow-up to send plan as sampled blob (only when sample=true).
Priya: After revert we should also trim retention TTL on detailed-annotations index so those inflated spans don't hang around. Retention currently 90d. Maybe reduce to 7d for this annotation sharded index.
Alex: Agree. Also add a guard in instrumentation to cap attr total size to 2KB per span and drop extras with a flag.
Jia: Create an eval to measure exporter CPU vs avg span size for different batching configs. We need data so next time we can auto-suggest correct batch_bytes.
Priya: I'll capture a pprof of exporter process during load test once revert is live.
Marcos: Revert PR merged and rolling. deploy-bot: rolled out reverse change instrumentation/service-x v2.11.3 -> v2.11.2 to 6 pods.
telemetry-bot: [info] exporter CPU dropping on full rollout, write_latency_p99 down to 110ms cluster-wide.
Alex: Great. Postmortem followups: 1) add attr-size telemetry metric, 2) autosuggest batch_bytes via Optimize, 3) add instrumenter lint to catch large serializations.
Jia: I'll draft the followup RFC and add owners.
Priya: Posting logs & pprof links in #eng-platform-attachments. :thumbsup:
Marcos: Sorry for the churn — learned to not serialize plan objects by default.
Alex: No blame — good catch and quick mitigation.
